To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a coherent European policy and law for space procurement is feasible and desirable and that the Third Way in European procurement law and policy provides an appropriate framework to achieve this.

the European Union and European Space Agency should: (1) develop a coherent policy framework for space procurement that takes into account both the specificities of the sector and the need to ensure a level playing field between Member States; (2) use the toolbox for space procurement to ensure that the European Union, European Space Agency and Member States procure in an effective and efficient way; (3) use the Extra-Procurement Tools to achieve the objectives of the European space policy.
- A Third Way is necessary to ensure coherence between European Space Agency (ESA) and European Union (EU) procurement policies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: 1.

(i) a coherent European space procurement policy; (ii) the European Space Agency and European Union procurement rules; (iii) extra-procurement instruments; and (iv) the role of Member States in space procurement.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the European space sector should adopt a coherent approach to procurement, but one that is flexible and pragmatic enough to cater for the specificities of the space sector.

a coherent European procurement law and policy for the space sector can only be achieved if the EU, the ESA and the Member States agree on a common set of principles, objectives, rules and procedures.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a Third Way is possible.

the EU and ESA are in the position of a "chicken and egg" situation: the EU is the chicken that needs to be hatched in order to lay the first egg (the ESA) which in turn is needed to hatch more chickens.
the EU should not be afraid to take a leading role in space procurement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EU and ESA have to work together to develop a coherent procurement policy for the space sector.
there is no one-size-fits-all solution to the challenges of public procurement in the space sector.

the European Union and European Space Agency should not only be able to act in parallel but should be able to act together, and that the European Union should not be excluded from the procurement process of European Space Agency programmes.
